title: Side jobs, no unions, and the show's route to St. Louis
summary: Musicians picked up party gigs and bootleg joints after shows with Moon's blessing; there were no unions, and the show reached Brooklyn and Lovejoy, Illinois near St. Louis.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Did you ever go and jam with any other musicians...?

Oh, man, that was the good part about it. And once in a while, not only the poor people would come to these medicine shows; some people would come there that had a little money. Some of these town people had a little money. Then some guy would once in a while say, "Could you play for a little party for us or something? You're going to be here a whole week. I'll hire you to play for a party, and give you five dollars a piece." And we did that, and if we wasn't doing that, we was always looking for a bootlegging joint.
And Doc Moon wouldn't mind you going to play with another band?
Oh, no! When we got through, that was it.
I was going to ask you this. Was there any unions in those days of musicians?

I never joined a union until I left... Well, I'll come around to that. But I stayed on Doc Moon's Medicine Show through St. Louis, went to St. Louis, and we played across the river from...right across the (?) called Brooklyn, Illinois, and Lovejoy, Illinois. And that's where Fate Marable used to play on the St. Paul; he used to play on the excursion boats. The boats was out of season at the time I was around St. Louis. But Charlie Creath stayed in St. Louis around about that time, and people used to... The Streckfus Brothers used to rent a thing out for excursions...
